solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Relish visiting Devizes today

indicators.note: the answer is visiting, staying inside, the words Devizes today, spanning their junction

explanation.surface: Someone enjoying a trip to the Wiltshire market town of Devizes.
explanation.walkthrough: Devizes is a town in Wiltshire; the letters sit across the end of one word and the start of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is gusto or keen enjoyment, a synonym of relish as a noun.

clue.text: Greek god mysteriously poisoned

indicators.note: mysteriously suggests the letters of poisoned are rearranged in some unexplained way

explanation.surface: A deity of Greek myth has been poisoned in strange circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysteriously' signals an anagram of POISONED.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek sea god, an example of a Greek deity.

clue.text: Ring about last letters from brave English nurse

indicators.note: about means the phone-call word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
the final two letters of the word brave are V and E

explanation.surface: Calling a courageous English nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the phone-call word round the final pair of 'brave'. Edith Cavell was a British nurse executed in 1915 for helping Allied soldiers escape occupied Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Cavell, the heroic First World War nurse, was famous for her courage in occupied Belgium.

clue.text: Arsonist springing out of tree, one wearing rubber

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree

indicators.note: wearing means one piece is clothed by the other, so the numeral sits inside

parts.note: a rubber is the British word for an eraser
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A fire-starter leaps from a tree while a figure wears rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts I inside ERASER. 'springing out of' is the link, the answer arising from the pieces; a rubber in Britain is a pencil eraser.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raiser is the British term for someone who deliberately sets fires, an arsonist.

clue.text: US soldiers meeting pensioner to get dope

parts.note: GI Joes, or joes, are American soldiers
OAP is old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: American troops meet an old man to buy drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP is the British abbreviation for an old-age pensioner. 'Dope' looks like drugs, but it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Soap is British slang for an ordinary, gullible person, a dope or mug.

clue.text: Novelist's delight over church

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece stands over the next one

parts.note: delight is a synonym of joy
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A writer's pleasure in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': Novelist is delight over church. James Joyce was the Irish author of Ulysses.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce was an Irish novelist, author of Ulysses and Finnegans Wake.

clue.text: Albert, for example, arranged prison concert

indicators.note: arranged suggests musical arrangement, and here the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone like Albert set up a concert in a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' signals an anagram of PRISON CONCERT. Albert was Queen Victoria's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert held the title of consort as husband of the reigning Queen Victoria.

clue.text: In the morning, around ten after ten, in truth

indicators.note: around means the morning abbreviation encloses the tens

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

indicators.note: after places the first-named ten behind the second

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
ten written in digits is 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Something true is said at about ten past ten in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten appears twice: first as the Roman numeral, then as 10 read as letters, the second placed 'after' the first and both set 'around' by the morning abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident statement accepted as true, a basic truth.

clue.text: Charming wise men, mostly quiet

parts.note: the Magi are the three wise men of the Nativity

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word for quiet is used, its final letter lost

parts.note: calm means quiet and still

explanation.surface: Delightful wise men who are, for the most part, peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of CALM, leaving CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Magical can mean enchanting or delightful, so it is a synonym of charming.

clue.text: An evergreen's required? Try elm, incorrectly

indicators.note: incorrectly tells us the letters of try elm are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Looking for an evergreen tree, someone suggests an elm by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' signals an anagram of TRY ELM; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with glossy leaves and fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Canned beer and cigs for cold, unemotional types

indicators.note: canned is slang for drunk, so the letters reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: Tins of beer and cigarettes kept in a cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' signals an anagram of BEER and CIGS together; 'and' is no fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg is figuratively a cold, aloof person who shows no feeling.

clue.text: Stop one about a line in magazine

parts.note: a full stop is called a period
one is the Roman numeral I
CA is circa, Latin for about
L is short for line

explanation.surface: Halt someone writing a line in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: CA (circa) is the abbreviation for about, used with dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodical is a publication issued at regular intervals, such as a magazine.

clue.text: Takes off, engaged in topping sport

indicators.note: engaged in means the rearranged letters are held within the cake topping

parts.note: icing is a topping for a cake

indicators.note: off means the letters of takes go wrong, out of order

explanation.surface: An excellent sport takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges 'Takes' and 'engaged in' sets those letters within the cake coating. 'Topping' looks like 'excellent' but is the cake coating.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice-skating, gliding on blades over ice, is a recreational and competitive sport.

clue.text: Roguish (paper version Shrewd) tramp, not married

indicators.note: not tells us the abbreviation for married is dropped

parts.note: to tramp is to march, walking heavily

explanation.surface: A cheeky vagrant who has never wed.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper version read 'Shrewd' for 'Roguish'; both fit. 'Tramp' looks like a vagrant noun but means to march.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means mischievous or knowingly playful, as in an arch look, which is roguish.

clue.text: Barrister from New York borough getting Eastern consul off

parts.note: Queens is one of the five boroughs of New York City

indicators.note: off means the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A lawyer from New York sees an Eastern diplomat leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of E plus CONSUL, giving the second word. A QC is a senior British barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: A Queen's Counsel is a senior barrister appointed in Britain under a queen.

clue.text: Question ruler abroad about a row

indicators.note: about means the rearranged ruler goes around the letter A
abroad suggests wandering away, so ruler's letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A foreign ruler is questioned in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' makes URREL from RULER and 'about' wraps it round A, giving UARREL after Q.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is an angry argument, which is a row in British usage.

clue.text: Ahead, master swimming against the current

parts.note: to be up is to be ahead, as in a game

indicators.note: swimming means the letters of master move about

explanation.surface: A master swimmer forges ahead against the flow of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' signals an anagram of MASTER, giving STREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstream means moving towards a river's source, against the current.

clue.text: Device used for raising a flag

definitions.meaning: a tool for lifting a car to change a wheel
a ship's small flag flown at the bow, as in Union ___

explanation.definitionFit: A jack lifts heavy loads, and a jack is also a naval flag such as the Union one.

clue.text: Powerful men meet leaving station

parts.note: kings are powerful rulers
paths that meet cross each other

explanation.surface: Mighty men gather before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' is the link. KING'S CROSS is a major London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: King's Cross is a mainline railway terminus in north London.

clue.text: Essential part of service in lower part of ship

indicators.note: in places the naval abbreviation inside the bottom timber

parts.note: the keel runs along a ship's bottom
RN is the Royal Navy, an armed service

explanation.surface: Something vital about service below decks.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the central or most important part of something, its core.

clue.text: Bird flying

definitions.meaning: a fast aerial bird with long narrow wings
moving very fast, as in a flying visit

explanation.definitionFit: The swift is a fast bird, and swift means speedy, as flying does.

clue.text: Rings about ending in 'Esther' and a trio performing in 'Deborah', say

indicators.note: about means the two rings go around the rest

parts.note: rings are the round letter O, two of them

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of Esther
performing suggests the trio putting on a show, their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A trio performs in Handel works such as Esther and Deborah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges 'a trio', and 'about' puts the last letter of Esther plus that inside two rings. Esther and Deborah are both Handel oratorios.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's Deborah is an oratorio, a sacred choral work for soloists, choir and orchestra.

clue.text: Chatter with minister, leader in temple

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish minister of religion

indicators.note: leader in picks the first letter of temple

explanation.surface: A gossip with a clergyman at the head of a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is informal British for talking at length, chattering.

clue.text: Try hard to support graduates

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece props up the one above

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, so BAs are graduates
H is short for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Making a big effort to back up graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try hard' looks like the definition, but hard is H.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a bash at something is to try it, an informal attempt.

clue.text: Weapon that gives clean wound

definitions.meaning: a long spear used by mounted knights
to pierce a boil or wound to drain and clean it

explanation.surface: A blade that inflicts a neat cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a cavalry spear; to lance a boil is to cut it open to clean it.

clue.text: Male not in to send out shipment

indicators.note: not in means the male abbreviation is not to be found within

parts.note: to transmit is to send out a signal

explanation.surface: A man who is absent sends goods out.
explanation.walkthrough: TRANSMIT loses M to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the carrying of goods from one place to another, shipment.
